title: Concurrency, CPU allocation and what cold start actually costs

videos.script: Three settings decide most of what a Cloud Run service costs and how fast it feels. This lesson sets them in order. {{concurrency}} First, concurrency. One instance can carry many requests at once, eighty by default. You will measure what yours can really carry, and where it stops. {{cpu}} Then the CPU. By default it is there only during a request. That is cheap for a service that idles, and it quietly breaks work done after the response. You will work out where the other billing becomes cheaper. {{cold}} Then the cold start. Most of it is your own program, before it listens. A big import can cost more than the container. {{minimum}} Last, the two ways to hide what is left. A warm minimum instance, and a faster processor at start-up. Both cost something, and you will see how much.
